title: Wars of Rome
summary: The Roman Republic's great wars of survival and expansion — from Hannibal's invasion of Italy to Caesar's conquest of Gaul.

stories.title: Hannibal's War
stories.summary: Hannibal Barca crosses the Alps and shatters Roman armies in Italy — until Scipio turns the war against Carthage itself.

events.title: Siege of Saguntum
events.body: Hannibal besieged the allied city of Saguntum on the Spanish coast, ignoring Roman demands to withdraw. Its fall after eight months gave Rome the casus belli for the Second Punic War.

events.title: Crossing the Alps
events.body: Hannibal led an army of roughly 40,000 men — war elephants included — over the Alpine passes into Italy. The march cost him half his force but achieved total strategic surprise.

events.title: Battle of Lake Trasimene
events.body: Hannibal ambushed the Roman consul Flaminius on the wooded shores of Lake Trasimene at dawn. In the fog and narrow terrain, 15,000 Romans were killed or captured in a few hours.

events.title: Battle of Cannae
events.body: Facing a Roman army twice his size, Hannibal deliberately weakened his centre and let it bend backward. The Roman legions pushed in — and his wings closed around them in a double envelopment that annihilated perhaps 50,000 men.

events.title: Battle of Zama
events.body: Scipio Africanus invaded North Africa and forced Hannibal to fight on Carthaginian soil. Roman cavalry drove off the Carthaginian horse, and Scipio's disciplined infantry broke Hannibal's veterans — ending the war.

stories.title: Caesar in Gaul
stories.summary: Julius Caesar conquers Gaul in eight years of campaigning — and crosses the Rubicon on his return.
